newsitem.title: USA: Wall St bonuses can create dissension - NY Times.
newsitem.headline: Wall St bonuses can create dissension - NY Times.

text.p: As Wall Street pre-tax profits are estimated to set a record $11.5 billion in 1996, executives are squabbling over how year-end bonuses should be divided, the New York Times reported on Sunday.
Most firms are planning increases of 30 percent to 40 percent, but Wall Street executives are looking at their bonuses compared to others, the paper said.
"Everybody knows what bonus everybody else got, and you are treated accordingly for the next 12 months," an unnamed managing director at a Wall Street firm told the paper.
Many firms lavish bonus guarantees to top traders, analysts and investment bankers to keep them loyal to the company, the paper said.

Many long-time employees at the firms are not happy with the huge bonuses paid to younger bankers and traders, while many younger executives fume about getting passed over for promotions, the paper said.

Traders in fixed income securities fret over the gaps in bonuses paid to stock traders and mergers and acquisitions bankers, the paper said. Also, some American executives are envious of the bonuses paid by European investment banks, the paper said.
